raw_text:
Principal objectives and general duties of Secretary of State and economic regulator
(1) The principal objectives of the Secretary of State and the GEMA in carrying out their respective functions under this Part are to—
(a)protect the interests of current and future transport and storage network users.
(b)protect the interests of any consumers whose interests the Secretary of State or the economic regulator (as the case may be) considers may be impacted by the exercise of their respective functions under this Part.
(c)promote the efficient and economic development and operation of transport and storage networks, having regard to the need for license holders to be able to finance their licensable activities.
(2) In this Part the GEMA is referred to as the “economic regulator”.
(3) The Secretary of State and the economic regulator must carry out their respective functions under this Part in the manner which the Secretary of State or the economic regulator (as the case may be) considers is best calculated to further the principal objectives, wherever appropriate by—
(a)promoting effective competition between persons engaged in, or in commercial activities connected with, the activities mentioned in section 2(2);
(b)promoting the resilience of transport and storage networks.
(c)protecting the public from dangers arising from the construction, operation and decommissioning of infrastructure used for the purposes of activities mentioned in section 2(2).
simplified_text:
Principal Objectives:
Users: They need to look out for the interests of people who currently use, and who will use in the future, the transport and storage networks.
Protect Consumers: They should also protect the interests of consumers who might be affected by their decisions and actions under this law.
Promote Efficiency and Economy: They should encourage the development and operation of transport and storage networks in an efficient and economical way. This includes making sure that the companies who hold licenses for these activities have enough money to carry them out.
General Duties:
The Secretary of State and the economic regulator must perform their duties in a way that they believe will best achieve these objectives. This may include:
Encouraging Competition: Promoting competition among companies involved in the transport and storage networks or related commercial activities.
Ensuring Resilience: Making sure that transport and storage networks are robust and reliable.
Protecting the Public: Safeguarding the public from any dangers that might arise from building, operating, or decommissioning infrastructure related to these networks.

raw_text:
Monitoring, information gathering etc

(1) The economic regulator must keep under review the carrying on in the United Kingdom and elsewhere of the following activities—

(a)operating a site for the disposal of carbon dioxide by way of geological storage.

(b)providing a service of transporting carbon dioxide by a licensable means of transportation.

(c)activities ancillary to activities mentioned in paragraph (a) or (b).

(2) The economic regulator may, for the purpose of facilitating the performance of its functions under this Part, collect information with respect to such activities.

(3) The economic regulator must give the Secretary of State or the CMA any information they may request with respect to any matter relating to the economic regulator’s functions under this Part.
simplified_text:
Review Activities: The economic regulator must regularly check and assess activities in the UK and possibly abroad regarding:

The operation of sites for burying carbon dioxide underground (geological storage).

The service of transporting carbon dioxide using methods that require a license.

Any additional activities that support the above two points.

Collect Information: For the purpose of doing its job well, the economic regulator can gather information about these activities.

Share Information: The economic regulator must provide information to the Secretary of State or the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) if they ask for it, as long as it's about something related to the regulator's duties in this area.

raw_text:
Power to create license types.

(1)The Secretary of State may by regulations provide that different types of license may be granted under section 7(1) in respect of different descriptions of activity falling within section 2(2).

(2) Regulations under this section may make consequential, transitional, incidental or supplementary provision including—

(a)amendments (or repeals or revocations) in any provision of this Act or any other enactment, and

(b)provision modifying any standard conditions of licences or provision determining the conditions which are to be standard conditions for the purposes of new types of licences.

(3) Before making regulations under this section containing provision within devolved competence, the Secretary of State must give notice to each relevant devolved authority—

(a)stating that the Secretary of State proposes to make regulations under this section, and

(b)specifying the period (of not less than 28 days from the date on which the notice is given) within which representations may be made with respect to the provision within the relevant devolved competence,

and must consider any representations duly made and not withdrawn.
simplified_text:
Creating Different License Types: The Secretary of State can set up different categories of licenses for various kinds of activities. These activities are the ones mentioned under a specific section of the law.

Making Additional Provisions: In setting up these licenses, the Secretary of State can also make additional rules. These could include changes to existing laws, setting conditions for these new licenses, or modifying the standard conditions for licenses.

Consulting Devolved Authorities: If the regulations affect areas under the control of devolved authorities (like Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland), the Secretary of State must inform these authorities. They must provide at least 28 days for these authorities to respond and must consider any feedback they receive.
